issues.legal_issue: A locality-wide preliminary acquisition notification may support only one subsequent declaration identifying land for acquisition in the ordinary acquisition process.
material_facts: A preliminary notification identified a locality as likely to be needed for a public purpose without specifying all particular parcels to be acquired.
Several declarations had already been issued under that preliminary notification for different land in the locality, and some land had been acquired.
A later declaration sought to acquire additional land in the same locality under the original preliminary notification.
The case did not involve the distinct urgency circumstances that might permit separate treatment of different categories of land.
issues.conclusion: The preliminary notification was exhausted by the earlier declaration or declarations and could not support the later declaration. The appeal was dismissed and the later declaration was quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4, 5-A and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, read together, establish a connected process: a preliminary notification identifies a locality, the survey and objection process enables the government to determine the particular land required, and one declaration identifies that land. The preliminary notification serves its purpose and is exhausted when that declaration is made; further acquisition in the locality requires a fresh preliminary notification. Babu Barkya Thakur v. State of Bombay, [1961] 1 SCR 128, is relied on for the distinction between the preliminary investigation under section 4 and the firm declaration under section 6. Sections 17 and 49 address special situations and do not establish a general power to issue successive declarations; section 48 does not make withdrawal under that section the only way a preliminary notification can cease to have effect, particularly given the power to rescind a notification under section 21 of the General Clauses Act, 1897.

rule.if: land_acquisition_appeal and locality_wide_preliminary_notice and earlier_declaration_under_same_notice and later_declaration_for_other_land_under_same_notice and ordinary_acquisition_process

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the validity of a declaration in a land acquisition process.
predicates.locality_wide_preliminary_notice: The acquiring authority issued a preliminary notice identifying a locality in which land might be needed, without identifying all particular land to be acquired.
predicates.earlier_declaration_under_same_notice: The acquiring authority had already issued a final declaration identifying land for acquisition under that preliminary notice.
predicates.later_declaration_for_other_land_under_s: The acquiring authority later attempted to declare additional land in the same locality for acquisition under the same preliminary notice.
predicates.ordinary_acquisition_process: The acquisition did not involve distinct urgent circumstances requiring separate treatment of different categories of land.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an ordinary acquisition in which a locality-wide preliminary notice has already supported a declaration and is then used for a later declaration of other land, the later declaration is invalid because the notice has been exhausted.
